ai.description: *Ophisops microlepis* is a small lacertid reaching 5 cm snout-vent length. It is brown with two distinct pale dorsolateral stripes and possesses fused eyelids forming a transparent spectacle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ophisops microlepis* is best distinguished by its lack of lower eyelids (transparent palpebral disc) and the presence of distinctly keeled, overlapping scales on the flanks.
ai.habitat: *Ophisops microlepis* inhabits dry, open grasslands and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate altitudes in rocky or sandy terrain.
ai.behavior: *Ophisops microlepis* is a diurnal lizard that actively forages for small insects by darting rapidly across open, sun-exposed rocky terrain.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ophisops microlepis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ophisops microlepis* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the dry, open scrublands and grasslands of central and western India.
